newsitem.title: USA: Danka CEO sees Kodak deal helping profits.
newsitem.headline: Danka CEO sees Kodak deal helping profits.

text.p: Danka Business Systems Plc's $684 billion purchase of Eastman Kodak Co's copier business will add to Danka earnings in the first year after closing, Danka Chief Executive Dan Doyle said on Monday.

He declined to detail the benefits during a telephone conference with reporters, but another Danka executive said precise forecasts on expected profits would be distributed to Danka shareholders during October.
Danka, a distributor of business products, will have a one-time restructuring charge of $25-$35 million against third-quarter profits, Doyle said.
"We also expect this to be accretive to earnings in the next 12 months," Doyle said.
The Kodak deal, coming after an extended sales effort by Kodak, will add to Kodak profits immediately after closing, expected by year-end, Kodak said.

Doyle said the transaction and an ongoing alliance with Kodak, which is keeping its manufacturing businesses in copiers, will give Danka a full line of products and services to compete against segment leader Xerox Corp.
